title: SQL Querying & Analysis
description: Write, debug, and optimise SQL queries for real analytical work. Tests GROUP BY logic, window functions, joins, and query performance.

seo.overviewTitle: SQL Data Querying, Joins & Advanced Aggregations
seo.overviewBody: SQL is the foundational language for data extraction and business analytics. Hiring managers evaluate data analysts on writing multi-table JOINs, GROUP BY aggregations, CTEs (Common Table Expressions), subqueries, and window functions (ROW_NUMBER(), RANK(), LAG()) to answer real business questions accurately.

deliverables.title: 1. Relational SQL Query Library
deliverables.desc: Structured SQL script file containing multi-table JOINs, aggregation metrics, and CTE queries.

deliverables.title: 2. Query Performance & Execution Analysis
deliverables.desc: Execution plan breakdown explaining index usage, JOIN optimization, and subquery refactoring.

deliverables.title: 3. Executive Data Insights Summary
deliverables.desc: Business report translating raw SQL metric results into actionable stakeholder recommendations.

faqs.question: What is the difference between WHERE and HAVING in SQL?
faqs.answer: WHERE filters rows before aggregations are processed, whereas HAVING filters aggregate results after GROUP BY execution.

faqs.question: When should you use Window Functions over GROUP BY?
faqs.answer: GROUP BY collapses multiple rows into a single summary row, while Window Functions calculate metrics (like running totals or lead/lag values) across row partitions without reducing the overall row count.

faqs.question: How do you prevent duplicate rows during multi-table LEFT JOINs?
faqs.answer: Ensure the joined key has a unique constraint, or use subqueries/CTEs to pre-aggregate the joined table before performing the main JOIN operation.
